name: BQ24166RGER
title: bq24165/bq24166/bq24167: 2.5 A dual-input single-cell Li-ion switch-mode charger with power-path management
summary: A one-cell Li-ion and Li-polymer charger built round a 1.5 MHz synchronous buck converter with its switches inside. It has two isolated supply inputs, IN (up to 2.5 A, overvoltage trip at 10.5 V) and USB (up to 1.5 A, trip at 6.5 V), with IN taking priority; both survive 20 V. The converter feeds a system rail SYS, and an internal FET from SYS to BAT charges the cell and lets the cell top up the system, so the system starts at once with a flat or missing battery; SYS is held at no less than about 3.5 V. Charge current, IN current limit and the IN input-voltage DPM point are set with resistors. The bq24165 takes two host inputs (CE1, CE2) to cut charge current or voltage for JEITA; the bq24166 watches a pack NTC for hot and cold; the bq24167 adds the warm and cool JEITA bands. Packages are a 2.8 mm 49-ball WCSP (YFF) and a 4 mm 24-pin VQFN (RGE).
key_figures: 550 mA to 2500 mA, set by RISET
4.2 V typ (4.179 to 4.221 V at 25 °C); 4.06 V reduced setting
4.2 V to 10 V operating, 18 V max recommended; OVP 10.5 V typ; current limit 1000 to 2500 mA by RILIM
4.2 V to 6 V operating; OVP 6.5 V typ; 100/150/500/800/900/1500 mA limits

notes: The three devices differ in how battery temperature reaches the charger: the bq24165 has the CE1 and CE2 selector inputs driven by a host; the bq24166 has a TS input with hot and cold limits; the bq24167 has a TS input with hot, warm, cool and cold limits. The bq24166 and bq24167 have a single CE enable input.
YFF is the 49-ball WCSP, RGE the 24-pin QFN. An R suffix is a 3000-piece reel, a T suffix a 250-piece reel.

pins.name: ISET

pins.name: DRV

pins.name: PG

circuits.title: bq24165 with external discharge FET and a GSM PA on SYS
circuits.description: The bq24165 runs from either a DC adapter on IN or a USB port on USB, each with a small input capacitor and a 4.7 µF capacitor on its PMID node. A divider from IN sets the IN DPM voltage, RILIM the IN current limit and RISET the charge current. The buck stage drives the system rail through the inductor, with a 0.01 µF bootstrap capacitor and 10 µF on SYS. A P-channel FET gated by BGATE parallels the internal battery FET for discharge. A GSM power amplifier hangs on SYS, so a call can go out with the battery flat or absent. The host reads the pack thermistor itself and drives CE1, CE2 and IUSB1 to IUSB3 from GPIOs; PG and CHG light LEDs fed from DRV.

operation.text: Charge current flows through the internal battery FET. Six control loops act on it: constant current, constant voltage, input current, die temperature, minimum system voltage and input-voltage DPM; whichever asks for least wins. Once the battery is above 3.5 V, SYS is joined to the battery. Below that, SYS is held at VSYS(REG), so the system runs even with a missing or deeply flat cell. A charge passes through conditioning, then constant current, then constant voltage.

A fixed 1.5 MHz voltage-mode synchronous buck with internal compensation, stable with small low-ESR ceramic output capacitors. The input stage blocks battery current back to a supply lower than the battery and keeps the two inputs apart. DRV powers the gate drivers, and a bootstrap capacitor lifts the high-side gate drive. Each input has a cycle-by-cycle limit of nominally 5 A peak, sensed in the internal FETs, plus its own input current limit.

With a supply present and a deeply discharged or shorted cell attached, the charger feeds 50 mA (IBATSHRT) into it while the battery FET runs linearly to keep SYS at VSYS(REG). Above VBATSHRT the current steps up to the fast-charge setting, still through the linear FET, until SYS would rise above VSYS(REG); then the FET turns fully on and the ISET current flows. If the input is at its current limit or DPM, charge current is cut first to serve the system; at zero charge current the battery begins to supplement SYS. The rise of fast-charge current is slew-limited. Near VBATREG the constant-voltage loop takes over and the current tapers; the voltage is sensed between BAT and PGND.

Charge ends, and the battery FET opens, when the cell sits over the recharge level and the tapering current has stayed below ITERM for 32 ms without a supplement event. Termination is held off while SYS is above VMINSYS and charge current is being cut by VINDPM, the input current loop, thermal regulation, or USB100 mode. After termination SYS is regulated at the battery regulation voltage and supplement mode stays available. Charging resumes when the battery drops below VBAT(REG) − VRCH, on supply power-on reset, on toggling CE1/CE2 or CE, or on toggling high-impedance mode through the IUSB pins; only a supply POR or a battery swap starts a fresh cycle. A battery above VBOVP turns the buck off and the battery FET on so the cell can discharge.

When termination conditions are met, the charger sinks IDETECT from BAT for tDETECT. If the voltage holds above the detection level, a battery is present and the charger reports charge done. If not, it sources IBATSHRT for tDETECT, then sinks again, and keeps alternating until a battery is found or charging is turned off; finding one clears the fault and starts a new cycle. With termination off, detection is off.

operation.topic: Power path with a supply present
operation.text: With a source on IN or USB the buck starts and, if enabled, charging begins. Above 3.5 V battery the FET is fully on and SYS follows the battery; when SYS falls to VSYS(REG) the buck holds it there and the battery FET regulates charge current linearly. If SYS drops to VMINSYS the DPPM loop lowers charge current to keep the load supplied; once charge current reaches zero and the load still grows, the battery FET turns on and the cell supplements the load. Whenever DPPM trims charge current, the safety timer slows to half rate.

If the battery is above VBAT(REG), the battery FET opens and SYS is regulated to VSYSREG(FETOFF). At 5 % above regulation the battery OVP stops the converter and closes the battery FET to bleed the cell down.

IUSB1, IUSB2 and IUSB3 select 100, 150, 500, 800, 900 mA or 1.5 A (Table 1), covering USB 2.0, USB 3.0 and wall adapters. IUSB1 and IUSB2 both high shuts the buck down in high-impedance mode whatever is on the inputs. USB100 disables termination.

operation.topic: IN current limit and input priority
operation.text: RILIM from ILIM to ground sets the IN limit between 1000 mA and 2.5 A. When both inputs are valid, IN is used. The inputs stay isolated from each other; if IN is above its OVP trip while USB is valid, charging runs from USB with both USB and the battery cut off from IN.

With no supply, the internal battery FET is on, as in supplement mode, with no current regulation but a short-circuit limit. On reaching it the FET opens for the deglitch time, then closes to test whether the short is gone, repeating until it is.

BGATE drives an optional external P-channel FET between battery and SYS that shares the discharge current with the internal FET, giving a low-impedance discharge path. It is on with no valid supply and in high-impedance mode. The short-circuit limit does not protect the external FET.

A 6-hour timer starts with charging and covers the whole charge. If charge has not terminated when it runs out, charging stops and the battery FET opens. The fault clears by toggling CE1/CE2 (bq24165) or CE (bq24166/7), by high-impedance mode, by supply POR, or by a battery swap. In fast charge the timer runs at half rate while the system load, the input current loop, VINDPM, or thermal regulation reduces charge current, while CE1/CE2 reduce current or voltage, while the battery is below VBATSHORT, and while TS or CE1/CE2 put it in the JEITA warm or cold band. A new cycle, a CE toggle, or a thermal shutdown resets it.

DRV is a linear regulator feeding the internal drivers and up to 10 mA of outside load such as a status LED or a USB transceiver; it is at most 5.45 V. It runs while either IN or USB has a supply, and off below UVLO, when the supply is less than VSLP above the battery, and in thermal shutdown.

For systems where the host measures pack temperature, two host GPIOs on CE1 and CE2 halve the charge current, drop the regulation voltage to 4.06 V, or suspend charging (Table 2), so the NTC need not be shared between ICs and the host picks the temperature points. Suspending charge through CE1/CE2 leaves the buck running.

TS compares the voltage of a DRV-fed divider with the pack NTC against fractions of VDRV. The bq24166 checks cold (below 0 °C, VCOLD) and hot (above 60 °C, VHOT): outside them charging and the timers pause. The bq24167 adds cool (0 to 10 °C, VCOOL), where charge current is halved, and warm (45 to 60 °C, VWARM), where the regulation voltage drops 140 mV. RLO and RHI follow from the NTC's hot and cold resistances (Equations 3 and 4); on the bq24167 they then fix the warm and cool points (Equations 5 and 6).

Charge current is tapered once the junction reaches the regulation threshold (TREG, 120 °C typ) and reaches zero about 10 °C higher, after which the battery carries more of the system load. Above TSHUTDWN (165 °C typ) charging stops and the buck is disabled, and the timer resets; operation resumes about 10 °C lower.

With the supply above VUVLO but below VBAT + VSLP, the converter stops and the battery FET and BGATE turn on, so the battery is not drained into a missing supply. A new charge cycle starts once the supply rises above VBAT + VSLP.

If the source cannot carry the requested current, its voltage sags; at VIN_DPM (set by the IUSB pins on USB, by the VDPM divider on IN) the input current is cut to stop it sagging further. The VDPM divider uses 10 kΩ at the bottom. On the QFN a 10 pF to 100 pF capacitor from VDPM to ground may be added when the divider sits away from the pins and VDPM picks up noise.

On connection the charger loads the source with 30 mA (USB) or 75 mA (IN) for 32 ms. If the voltage stays above the VINDPM level plus hysteresis, the buck starts; if not, the sink stops for 2 s and tries again, indefinitely, until a good source appears on either input. A source that falls to the bad-source level in operation stops the converter and the battery FET turns on. With two supplies IN is tested first; one failure switches to USB for 2 s before retrying IN, and a second failure locks IN out until it drops below UVLO.
Above VOVP on the active input the converter stops, charging pauses, and the battery FET and BGATE turn on. The previous operation resumes when the overvoltage goes away.

The buck is held in continuous conduction even at light load for fast load response, so a battery above VBATREG could drive current back to the input and raise a source that cannot sink. When reverse current not caused by supplement mode is sensed, the battery FET opens and feedback moves to VSYSREG for 1 ms, then the FET closes and the test repeats. This is active only while VBOVP > VBAT > VBATREG − VRCH; with termination off in that window (for example CE1 = 1, CE2 = 0 with the cell above 4.06 V) it gives about 100 mV of 1 kHz ripple on SYS. Termination enabled with ITERM above 150 mA, or high battery-line impedance, makes it much less likely. A SYS load step that causes supplement during this state can stop charging, which resumes below VBATREG − VRCH, so large load steps can leave the cell a little short of full.

PG and CHG are open-drain. PG pulls low when the supply exceeds VUVLO and lies between VBAT + VSLP and VOVP. CHG goes low at the start of a new charge cycle (begun by a battery swap or supply cycling), and stays low through TS or thermal suspensions until termination, a battery removal, a timer fault or loss of supply; it does not go low for recharges. Either output can drive an LED from DRV or use a 100 kΩ pull-up to the logic rail.

The converter is meant for 1.5 µH to 2.2 µH. 2.2 µH has less ripple and a little more efficiency but is physically larger; 1.5 µH balances size and efficiency. Saturation current must exceed IPEAK (Equation 8), and the inductor's 40 °C-rise current must cover the duty-weighted load (Equation 9). Thanks to internal compensation, anywhere from 10 µF to 200 µF placed locally on SYS keeps the loop stable; more may sit further along the rail. 10 µF to 47 µF of ceramic is the local SYS bypass, 47 µF giving the best transient response.

Put the 4.7 µF PMID capacitors right at the PMID and PGND pins to keep the high-frequency loop small, and ground the 1 µF input capacitors close to the PMID capacitor ground and PGND. Keep BAT to the battery connector short; add BAT capacitance if its inductance is large. Return the SYS capacitor to PGND close to the IC so the SW–LC–PGND loop is small. Put the ISET and ILIM resistors at their pins and all decoupling close to its pin and PGND, without breaking the power-stage paths, and route small signals away from high current. Use a ground plane reached by vias: two per power-stage capacitor, one per small-signal capacitor, and vias in the PGND pads where possible; a single plane works for this layout. Size IN, USB, BAT, SYS and SW traces for full charge current, and on WCSP give the power balls as much copper as possible for heat.
The top of the YFF package carries the A1 corner mark, TI letters, a year-month date code, a four-character lot code, an assembly site code and the device name.
